name: workspace-keys
description: OpenAI-compatible chat models for VS Code, with API key, base URL and model list scoped per workspace.
author: Noser Engineering AG

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace no workspace settings are read and no network requests are made, so no models are contributed.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Providers and keys resolve from settings and SecretStorage, so no local filesystem access is required.

commands.title: Set or Update API Key for Current Workspace

workspaceKeys.providers.markdownDescription:
OpenAI-compatible endpoints. No endpoint ships with the extension: add the first one with **Workspace Keys: Add Provider Endpoint**, which writes it to your **user settings** so every workspace inherits it.

A single workspace can still override the whole list in `.vscode/settings.json`. Note that VS Code replaces array settings rather than merging them, so a workspace value replaces your user list entirely — and a workspace-declared endpoint has to be approved before anything is sent to it.

Give each workspace its own key with **Workspace Keys: Set or Update API Key for Current Workspace** (SecretStorage). The optional `apiKey` field below acts as the fallback for workspaces that have none — prefer `${env:NAME}` over a literal value.

id.description: Stable identifier for this provider. Used as part of the SecretStorage key, so changing it detaches a stored key. Must not contain '/'.

label.description: Human-readable name shown next to the models in the picker.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible API, for example https://api.example.com/v1. Must be https:// — cleartext http:// is only accepted for loopback hosts and only when the development setting 'Allow Insecure Loopback' is enabled.

apiKey.markdownDescription: Optional key source. Prefer `${env:NAME}` over a literal key; a literal value is stored in plain text and must not be committed.

models.description: Optional explicit model allowlist. If omitted, models are discovered from GET {baseUrl}/models.

headers.description: Additional HTTP headers sent with every request to this provider. Authentication, routing and framing headers (Authorization, Cookie, Host, Content-Type, Accept, …) are ignored and cannot be overridden.

workspaceKeys.requestDefaults.description: Default request parameters passed through to the provider.

enumDescriptions: Use the workspace folder of the active editor, falling back to the first folder.
Always use the first workspace folder.
workspaceKeys.multiRootResolution.description: How to pick the workspace folder whose configuration applies, in a multi-root workspace.

workspaceKeys.modelRules.markdownDescription:
Capability rules for discovered models, matched by glob against the model id. Applied after the built-in defaults, so these win. Broader patterns must come before narrower ones.

User-scoped on purpose: a workspace cannot override it and therefore cannot claim a capability a model does not have.

match.description: Glob matched against the model id. Supports * and ?.

toolCalling.description: Whether the model supports tool calling. A number sets the maximum number of tools per request. Required for agent mode.

imageInput.description: Whether the model accepts image input.

workspaceKeys.hideUnknownModels.description: Hide discovered models that no rule matches. When disabled, unmatched models are listed with conservative fallback capabilities and no tool calling.

workspaceKeys.allowInsecureLoopback.markdownDescription:
**Development only.** Allow cleartext `http://` endpoints on loopback hosts (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`), so a local mock provider can be used.

User-scoped on purpose: a workspace cannot enable it and therefore cannot downgrade the transport of an endpoint it declares. Remote `http://` endpoints stay rejected either way.
